intro.data: A coproduct is the mirror image of a product: instead of bundling both, it holds either one. A Payment is either Card or Cash. Given a way to handle each, build the single machine that handles a Payment.
intro.alchemy: A coproduct is the mirror image of a product: instead of bundling both, it holds either one. A Reagent is either Acid or Base. Given a way to handle each, build the single apparatus that handles a Reagent.
intro.spellcraft: A coproduct is the mirror image of a product: instead of bundling both, it holds either one. A Charm is either Ward or Hex. Given a way to handle each, build the single rune that handles a Charm.
intro.abstract: A coproduct A+B holds either an A or a B, with injections ι₁, ι₂. Given f : A→Y and g : B→Y, build [f,g] : A+B→Y.

goal.data: Wire the Payment through the single handler that covers both cases to the Receipt.
goal.alchemy: Wire the Reagent through the single handler that covers both cases to the Result.
goal.spellcraft: Wire the Charm through the single handler that covers both cases to the Effect.
goal.abstract: Wire A+B through [f,g] to reach Y.

afterSuccess.data: One handler covered both cases: a Card goes through chargeCard, a Cash through logCash, exactly as the case-split promises. The coproduct is the product turned around — injections in, one map out.
afterSuccess.alchemy: One handler covered both cases, exactly as the case-split promises. The coproduct is the product turned around — injections in, one map out.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: One handler covered both cases, exactly as the case-split promises. The coproduct is the product turned around — injections in, one map out.
afterSuccess.abstract: [f,g] handles both cases via the injections: [f,g]∘ι₁ = f and [f,g]∘ι₂ = g. The coproduct is the product with every arrow reversed.

reveal.summary: The universal property of the coproduct: for any f : A→Y and g : B→Y there is a unique [f,g] : A+B→Y with [f,g]∘ι₁ = f and [f,g]∘ι₂ = g.
reveal.moreFormal: Coproduct is the dual of product: reverse every arrow in the product's universal property and you get the coproduct's. Products are 'and'; coproducts are 'or'.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: type Payment = Card | Cash; match it: (p) => p.kind === 'card' ? f(p) : g(p).
